experiment: ESS2 — black copper inside a hot-sand cavity (front also surrounded by hot store; light enters through a small aperture)
status: pre-registered after ESS1 (whose P2 failed: the front face radiated the store's heat to the sky at night) and before running ess2_run.py
logic: For the author's condition 'the interior is all hot, so heat does not leave easily' to hold, the absorber's front must also face hot surroundings. That is a cavity receiver: black copper lines a cavity inside the hot sand; sunlight concentrated by ratio CR enters through an aperture of area A_coll/CR; re-radiation and convection leave only through the aperture; the aperture is closed at night (shutter).

model.irradiance: same as ESS1 (800 W/m^2 peak, 8 h sine day)
model.cavity_effective_absorptance: alpha_eff = alpha / (alpha + (1 - alpha) * A_ap / A_cav) with alpha = 0.96, A_cav / A_ap = 20 (standard cavity-receiver relation)
model.aperture_loss: eps_ap = 1 (an open aperture radiates as a black body) x sigma x (T^4 - T_sky^4) x A_ap + h = 10 x A_ap x (T - T_amb), daytime only; aperture shuttered at night
model.store: same as ESS1: C = 1.40 MJ/K, insulation UA = C / 5.4 days

predictions.P1_accumulates: for CR >= 50 the store keeps accumulating over 30 days (store T at day 30 exceeds day 5 by > 50 K)
predictions.P2_beats_ESS1: for every CR >= 10, 30-day stored energy exceeds ESS1's best case (8.6 kWh)
predictions.P3_limit_is_insulation: for CR >= 50 the insulation (side) loss exceeds the aperture loss over 30 days, i.e. the hot surround has moved the bottleneck off the absorber
predictions.P4_CR1_no_rescue: at CR = 1 (no concentration, aperture = collector) the cavity does not rescue accumulation (day-30 minus day-5 < 50 K)

note: Heat collection and storage only. Black copper still has no heat-to-electricity mechanism; the Carnot limit at the reached store temperature is reported for a separate converter.
